# Regular expressions

Test text against a regular expression.

**Library:** [Standard library](index.md#standard-library), for apps and code-pipeline hooks. More in [Cogniscript](../../../concepts/cogniscript.md).

| Call | What it does |
|---|---|
| [`RegexIsMatch`](#regexismatch) | Whether a regular expression matches anywhere in text. |

### RegexIsMatch

Whether a regular expression matches anywhere in text.

```c
bool RegexIsMatch(string input, string pattern)
```

| Name | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `input` | `string` | The text to search. |
| `pattern` | `string` | The regular expression. |

**Returns** `bool`: `true` when `pattern` matches all or part of `input`.

Patterns use .NET regular expression syntax, with the default options: matching is case-sensitive, and `^` and `$` mean the start and end of the whole text, not of each line. A pattern can match any part of the text, so anchor it to test the whole text: `^[A-Z]{3}$`. Start the pattern with `(?i)` to ignore case, or `(?m)` to make `^` and `$` match at each line.

In a Cogniscript string a backslash must be written twice: the pattern `^\d+$` is written `"^\\d+$"`. A single backslash before a letter that is not an escape, such as `d`, stops the app from compiling, and a single backslash before punctuation is dropped: `"a\.b"` becomes the pattern `a.b`, which also matches `axb`.

Raises an error for an invalid pattern, such as `Invalid pattern '(' at offset 1. Not enough )'s.`
